newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Peace-broking U.S. envoy bids farewell to Sarajevo.
newsitem.headline: Peace-broking U.S. envoy bids farewell to Sarajevo.

text.p: The United States ambassador to Bosnia is to leave Sarajevo after two years of playing an important role in the peace process, embassy officials said on Sunday.
Bosnian government leaders and U.S. Assistant Secretary of State John Kornblum attended a farewell ceremony for outgoing Ambassador John Menzies on Saturday evening.
Kornblum, Washington's envoy to the Balkans, praised Menzies for his "heroic service" during the city's siege and for his work in U.S-sponsored peace talks in Dayton, Ohio last year.
He said the peace agreement was far from perfect but that it had stopped four years of bloodshed in former Yugoslavia.

"It's a complicated agreement that satisfied no one and that is perhaps why it succeeded. Nobody likes it but everyone is willing to live with it," said Kornblum, speaking on the first anniversary of the treaty signing.

Menzies said he believed the peace would hold and recalled a pivotal point at peace talks when Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic agreed to end the siege of Sarajevo, returning control of the whole city to the Bosnian government.
"I remember the fateful moment at Dayton when President Milosevic said to (Bosnian) Prime Minister (Haris) Silajdzic, 'You fought for Sarajevo for three years -- you've earned it.'
"And in that moment Sarajevo was reunited. But we still have a long way to go, " Menzies said.
Menzies worked in the Sarajevo embassy for a year before he was appointed ambassador in October 1995 by former Assistant Secretary of State Richard Holbrooke, the architect of the Dayton accords.
His successor has yet to be named but whoever replaces Menzies in the Sarajevo embassy will be at the centre of Washington's expensive efforts to implement the peace treaty.
